The Blessed One said: "O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, you should honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the more senior one. You should perform the acts of greeting, salutation, rising, joined palms, and proper conduct. He deserves to enjoy the foremost seat, foremost water, and foremost alms-food." The Blessed One said: "The senior <s>bhikṣu</s> should be honored by you." As before.

The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta</s>'s Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, a number of [<s>bhikṣu</s>s] seated and assembled in the attendance hall had this kind of discussion arise among them: "Whom, venerable ones, should we honor, respect, esteem, and venerate? To whom should we perform the acts of greeting, salutation, rising, joined palms, and proper conduct? Who among us deserves to enjoy the foremost seat, foremost water, and foremost alms-food?"

children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "The seasonal [ordination date] should be announced." The <s>bhikṣu</s>s did not know how many seasonal [dates] there were. The Blessed One said: "O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, there are five seasons: the winter season, the summer season, the rains season, the expired rains, and the extended rains. Of these: the winter season is four months; the summer season is four months; the rains season is one month; the expired rains is one day and night; the extended rains is three months minus one night. Thus, having announced the seasonal [ordination date], whoever was ordained first should be saluted.

children.translated_text: For all this world with its <s>Māra</s>s, its <s>Brahmā</s>s, with ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, with its gods and humans, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One is to be saluted. For all householders, those who have gone forth are to be saluted. For all fully ordained ones, those who were ordained earlier are to be saluted.

children.text: A 315a

children.translated_text:
Except for a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>: even one ordained a hundred years ago — a <s>bhikṣu</s> ordained that very day is to be saluted by her. For every unordained person, an ordained person is to be saluted.
Ten [types] are not to be saluted. Which ten? One undergoing probation (<s>pārivāsika</s>), one undergoing root-probation (<s>mūlapārivāsika</s>), one whose probation has expired, one undergoing the <s>mānāpya</s> discipline, one who has completed the <s>mānāpya</s>, one suspended for not acknowledging [an offense], one suspended for not making amends, one suspended for not renouncing a wrong view, every householder, and every unordained person.

The <s>bhikṣu</s>s, having arisen in doubt, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: "Look, venerable sir, when the Blessed One prescribed [seniority] by ordination-age, then the <s>bhikṣu</s>s honor, respect, esteem, and venerate one another. Honoring, respecting, esteeming, and venerating one another, they grow in wholesome <s>dharma</s>s like a lotus in water." The Blessed One said: "What wonder is there in this, O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, that now, when I, free from passion,

<s>Bhikṣu</s>s were honoring, respecting, esteeming, and venerating elderly householders. Hearing this, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-householders disparaged, criticized, and complained: "We are nobles, enjoyers of sensual pleasures, sunk in the mire of desire. Why do you honor us?" The <s>bhikṣu</s>s reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, I spoke intending those who have gone forth, not householders."
The <s>bhikṣu</s>s, seeing elderly adherents of other sects, were honoring, respecting, and esteeming them.

children.text: ) asti vayaṃ bhavantaḥ parasparaṃ sakhyenāvasthitāḥ sahitāḥ samagrāḥ saṃmodamānā avivadamānāḥ; kin tu na jānīmaḥ ko 'smābhiḥ satkartavyo gurukartavyo mānayitavyaḥ pūjayitavyaḥ iti; yan nu vayaṃ yathāvṛddhikāṃ prajñapayema iti; te parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kartum ārabdhā iti; ko 'smākaṃ vṛddha iti; tataḥ kapiṃjalena vaṭavṛkṣo darśitaḥ; bhavantaḥ eṣa vaṭavṛkṣaḥ kena kiyatpramāṇo dṛṣṭa iti; hastī kathayati; mayā yūthena sahānena pathā gacchatā ayaṃ dṛṣṭo matpramāṇa eva uccatveneti; markaṭaḥ kathayati; mayā yūthena sahānena pathā gacchatā ayaṃ dṛṣṭo mama tulya evoccatveneti; te kathayanti; tvam asya vṛddha iti; śaśaḥ kathayati; mayāpy asya dvipatrakasya patreṣv evāvaśyayanbindavo jihvayā nirlīḍhā iti; te kathayanti: tvam apy anayor vṛddha iti; kapiñjalaḥ kathayati; paśyata yūyam enaṃ vaṭavṛkṣaṃ mahatpramāṇākāram; te kathayanti: paśyāmaḥ; etasmān mayā phalāni bhakṣayitvāsmin pradeśe uccāraḥ kṛtas tasmād ayaṃ jāta iti; (
children.translated_text: ) 'Sirs, we dwell together in mutual friendship, united, harmonious, delighting in each other, without quarreling. But we do not know which of us should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated. Let us therefore establish a seniority order.' They began to confer with one another: 'Who among us is the eldest?' Then the partridge (<s>kapiñjala</s>) pointed out a banyan tree (<s>vaṭavṛkṣa</s>): 'Sirs, this banyan tree — who first saw it and at what size?' The elephant said: 'When I was going along this path with my herd, I saw it — it was just my height in tallness.' The monkey said: 'When I was young, sitting on the ground, I used to gnaw at the tips of this tree.' The hare said: 'When I was young, on a moonlit night in the rainy season, I ate the young leaves that had sprouted from the fallen fruit of this tree — therefore I am older than these two.' The partridge said: 'Sirs, on a certain mountain I ate a fruit and deposited a dropping here. From that this tree grew. If so, I am the eldest of all.' They asked: 'Is there anyone even older?' He said: 'There is no one older than me.'

children.translated_text: ) all living creatures down to the animals were established in the five precept-vows. Not harming one another, dwelling mindfully in that grove, they lived as they pleased. By their spiritual power, the rain god sent timely rains; the trees were always in flower and fruit; the earth was rich in crops. People observed them living without harming one another, the trees always in flower and fruit, the earth rich in crops. The king said: 'I rule the kingdom righteously — this is due to my power.' The inner palace, princes, ministers, soldiers and army commanders, merchants, and townsfolk said: 'This is due to our power.' They went to the forest grove and saw those four creatures dwelling without harming one another and all animals established in the five precepts. They asked: 'Who established you?' They replied: 'The partridge.' [The people asked:] 'Where does the partridge dwell?' They showed them. Having gone, they saw the partridge. Then the king, together with the inner palace, princes, ministers, soldiers, merchants, and townsfolk — all of them, having seen, honored and venerated the partridge. The king said: 'By the power of this partridge my kingdom prospers. Let an order be proclaimed by drumbeat throughout the <s>Kāśī</s> kingdom: None shall harm these four creatures; whoever harms them shall be punished by the king.' The order was proclaimed. By the power of the five precepts, those four, when they died, were reborn in the heavenly worlds.

children.text:
) nātyāsanne divā alpākīrṇo 'lpavilāpo rātrāv alpaśabdo 'lpanirghoṣaḥ alpadaṃśamaśakavātātapasarīsṛpasaṃsparśaḥ, yatrāhaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayiṣyāmīti; adrākṣīd anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ, jetasya kumarasyārāmam śrāvastyā nātidūre nātyāsanne divā alpākīṇam alpavilāpaṃ rātrāv alpaśabdṃ alpanirghoṣaṃ alpadaṃśamaśakavātātapasarīsṛpasparśam; dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyaitad abhavat: atrāhaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayiṣyāmīti; sa praviśann eva svaṃ niveśanaṃ yena jetaḥ kumāras tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya jetaṃ kumāram idam avocat; anuprayaccha me kumāra ārāmam; ahaṃ tatra bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ kārayāmi iti; sa kathayati; na me gṛhapate sa ārāmaḥ; kin tu udyānaṃ tan mameti; dvir api trir apy anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetaṃ kumāram idam avocat: anuprayaccha me kumāra ārāmam; ahaṃ tatra bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayāmīti; aparityakto ḥgṛhapateḥ me ārāmāḥ koṭisaṃstareṇāpi; punar apy anāthapiṇḍado gṛhaptir jetaṃ kumaram idam avocat: kṛtārgho 'si kumāra ārāmasya; pratīccha hiraṇyasuvarṇam; mamārāmaḥ; kaḥ kṛtārghaḥ? tvaṃ kṛtārghaḥ; tau kṛtārgho na kṛtargha iti vivādam āpannau, yena vyāvahārikapuruṣās tena saṃprasthitāḥ; atrāntare caturṇāṃ lokapālānām etad abhavat; ayam anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir udyukto bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ vihāraṃ māpayitum; sāhāyyam asyānuṣṭheyam iti; tato vyāvahārikapuruṣam ātmānam abhinirmāya
arthādhikaraṇe niṣaṇṇāḥ; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetaś ca kumāro vyāvahārikasakāśam upasaṅkrāntau; athānāthapiṇḍako gṛhapatir vyāvahārikapuruṣāṇām etam arthaṃ vistareṇa nivedayati; te kathayanti; kṛtārgho 'si kumāra ārāmasya; pratīccha suvarṇam: gṛhapatre ārāma iti; sa tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ śakaṭair bhāraiḥ mūṭaiḥ piṭakair uṣṭrair gobhir gardabhaiḥ prabhūtaṃ suvarṇam abhinirhṛtya, sarvaṃ jetavanaṃ saṃstartum ārabdhaḥ; na parisamāpyate; tiṣṭhate evānāstīrṇaḥ kaścit pṛthivīpradeśaḥ; tataḥ anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir etam arthaṃ cintayan muhūrtaṃ tūṣṇīm asthāt; katarat tan nidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati? nātistokaṃ, nātiprabhūtaṃ yena ayam anāstīrṇaḥ pṛthivīpradeśaḥ āstariṣyati; na ca punar gopayitavyo bhaviṣyatīti; jetaḥ kumāraḥ saṃlakṣayati; nūnam anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater vipratisāraḥ; kasmād ārāmakāraṇād iyantaṃ mahāntaṃ dhanaskandhaṃ parityajāmi; iti viditvā anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim idam (
children.translated_text: not too near [the city], by day sparsely frequented, with little chatter, by night with little sound, little commotion, few gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, heat, and contact with creeping things — where I shall build a monastery for the Blessed One.' The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> saw the park of Prince <s>Jeta</s> — neither too far from nor too near <s>Śrāvastī</s>, by day sparsely frequented, with little chatter, by night with little sound, little commotion, few gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, heat, and contact with creeping things. Having seen it, this thought occurred to him: 'Here I shall build a monastery for the Blessed One.' Entering his own residence, he approached Prince <s>Jeta</s>. Having approached, he said this to Prince <s>Jeta</s>: 'Give me, Prince, the park; I shall have a monastery built there for the Blessed One.' He [Jeta] said: 'That is not my park, householder; rather, it is my pleasure garden.' A second time and even a third time the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said this to Prince <s>Jeta</s>: 'Give me, Prince, the park; I shall build a monastery there for the Blessed One.' 'My parks are not to be parted with, householder — not even for carpeting [the ground] with ten million [coins].' Again the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said this to Prince <s>Jeta</s>: 'You have set a price for the park, Prince; accept the gold and silver — the park is mine!' 'Who set the price?' 'You set the price.' The two fell into a dispute — 'the price is set' versus 'the price is not set' — and proceeded to the arbitrators. Meanwhile, the Four World-Guardians (<s>Lokapālas</s>) thought: 'This householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> is exerting himself to build a monastery for the Blessed One; assistance should be rendered to him.' Then, having magically created themselves as arbitrators, they sat in the tribunal. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> and Prince <s>Jeta</s> approached the arbitrators. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> reported the matter in detail to the arbitrators. They said: 'You have set a price for the park, Prince; accept the gold — the park belongs to the householder.' He [Jeta] stood silent. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having brought out an abundance of gold by carts, loads, bundles, baskets, camels, oxen, and donkeys, began to cover all of <s>Jetavana</s> [with gold coins]. It was not completed — a certain piece of ground remained uncovered. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, pondering this matter, stood silent for a moment: 'Which treasury shall it be? Neither too small nor too large, by which this uncovered piece of ground will be covered, and yet [the treasury] will not need to be concealed.' Prince <s>Jeta</s> reflected: 'Surely the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> has regrets. Why would he give up such an immense mass of wealth for the sake of a park?' Having perceived this, he said this to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>:

children.text: Śay-v 20
children.translated_text: [Śay-v 20]

children.text: ) avocat; sacet te ha gṛhapate vipratisāraḥ pratīccha suvarṇam; mamaivārāmaḥ; na me kumāra vipratisāraḥ; api tv aham etam evārtham anucintayan muhūrtaṃ tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; katarat tan nidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati? nātistokaṃ nātiprabhūtaṃ, yenāyam anāstīrṇaḥ pṛthivīpradeśaḥ āstariṣyati; na ca punar gopayitavyo bhaviṣyatīti; atha jetasya kumārasya etad abhavat: na batāvaro buddho bhaviṣyati; nāvaraṃ dharmākhyānam; yatredānīm ayaṃ gṛhapatir ārāmakāraṇād iyantaṃ mahāntaṃ dhanaskandhaṃ parityajati; iti viditvā anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat: anuprayaccha me gṛhapate anāstīrṇaṃ pṛthivīpradeśam; atrāhaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ māpayāmi; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetasya kumārasya anāstīrṇaṃ pṛthivīpradeśam anuprayacchati; yatra jetaḥ kumāro bhagavato 'rthāya dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ māpayati
children.translated_text: 'If you have regrets, householder, take back the gold — the park is mine.' 'I have no regrets, Prince. Rather, I was standing silent for a moment pondering this very matter: Which treasury shall it be? Neither too small nor too large, by which this uncovered piece of ground will be covered, and yet [the treasury] will not need to be concealed.' Then this thought occurred to Prince <s>Jeta</s>: 'The <s>Buddha</s> must be no ordinary being; the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s> must be no ordinary thing — since this householder, for the sake of a park, gives up such an immense mass of wealth!' Having perceived this, he said this to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'Give me, householder, the uncovered piece of ground; there I shall build a gate-house (<s>dvārakoṣṭhaka</s>) for the Blessed One.' The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> gave the uncovered piece of ground to Prince <s>Jeta</s>, where Prince <s>Jeta</s> built a gate-house for the Blessed One.

Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, at the passing of that night, in the morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Having gone for alms in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, having finished his meal, having returned from his alms-round in the afternoon, [he set out] as assigned

children.text: athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayitum ārabdha iti tīvradveṣaparyākulīkṛtamanasas tīrthyās te saṃbhūya yenānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatis tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ; upasaṃkramya kathayanti: mā tvaṃ gṛhapate śramaṇasya gautamasya arthāyātra vihāraṃ kāraya; kiṃ kāraṇam? asmābhir nagarāṇi bhājitāni; śramaṇasya gautamasya rājagṛham; asmākaṃ śrāvastī; sa kathayati: bhājitāni yuṣmābhir nagarāṇi, na tu madīyam svāpateyam; yasyābhipretaṃ tasya dharmaskandhaṃ kārayāmīti; te rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ; tatrāpy anāthapiṇḍadena parājitāḥ; dhvāṅkṣās tīrthyā avikṛtavadanāḥ kathayanti; gṛhapate na te kāmakāram anuprayacchāmaḥ; śramaṇasya gautamasyāgraśrāvakaḥ āgataḥ; sa yady asmān vādena parājayate, kāraya vihāram iti; sa kathayati: śobhanam; āryaśāriputraṃ tāvad avalokayāmīti; athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir yenāyuṣmān śāriputraḥ tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramyāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ; ekantaniṣaṇṇo 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram idam avocat; tīrthyā bhadanta śāriputra evam āhuḥ; gṛhapate na te kāmakāram anuprayacchāmaḥ; śramaṇasya gautamasya agraśrāvaka āgataḥ; sa yady asmān vādena parājayate, kāraya vihāram iti; katham atra pratipattavyam iti; āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ saṃlakṣayati; kim eṣāṃ santi kānicit kuśalamūlāni uta na santīti; paśyati, santi; kasyāntike pratibaddhāni; mamaiva; punaḥ saṃlakṣayati; kim etāvanta eva mama pratibaddhā vineyā āhosvid anye 'pi vādena vineyāḥ santīti; paśyati, santi; kiyaccireṇa sannipatiṣyanti; (
Śay-v 24
children.translated_text: [Śay-v 24]

children.text:
) paśyati, saptāhasyātyayād iti; samanvāhṛtya kathayati: gṛhapate enaṃ bhavatu; kiṃ
tu saptame divase; tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ prītiprāmodyajāto yena tīrthyās tena upasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya tīrthyān idam avocat; bhadanta āryaśāriputraḥ kathatyati: śobhanam, evaṃ bhavatu; kiṃ tu saptame divase iti; te saṃlakṣayanti; dvābhyām atra kāraṇābhyām bhavitavyam; athavāsau niṣpalāyitukāmaḥ; athavā pakṣaṃ samanveṣṭukāmaḥ; kim atra prāptakālam; vayam api pakṣaṃ samanveṣāmaha iti; te pakṣaṃ samanveṣṭum ārabdhāḥ; taiḥ pakṣam samanveṣamānai raktākṣo nāma parivrājako dṛṣṭaḥ; sa tair uktaḥ; tvam asmākaṃ sabrahmacāri; śramaṇasya gautamasyāgraśrāvako 'smābhir vādenāhūtaḥ; sa pakṣaṃ samanveṣate; tvam asmākaṃ sāhāyyaṃ kalpaya; kiyatā kālena? itaḥ saptame divase; śobhanam, evaṃ bhavatu; yadā yuṣmākaṃ sannipato bhavati tadā mamārocayitavyam; tīrthyāḥ śaṅkitodvignamanaso divasānudivasaṃ pakṣaṃ samanveṣayante; divasāṃś ca gaṇayanti
children.translated_text: He saw: 'After the passage of seven days.' Having considered, he said: 'Householder, let it be so; but [we shall meet] on the seventh day.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, filled with joy and delight, approached the <s>Tīrthyas</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Tīrthyas</s>: 'Venerable ones, the noble <s>Śāriputra</s> says: "Very well, let it be so; but [we shall meet] on the seventh day."' They reflected: 'There must be one of two reasons for this: either he wishes to flee, or he wishes to search for allies. What is the proper course now? We too shall search for allies.' They began to search for allies. While searching for allies, they found a wanderer (<s>parivrājaka</s>) named <s>Raktākṣa</s> (Red-Eye). They said to him: 'You are our fellow celibate. The chief disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been challenged by us to debate. He is searching for allies. You must render us assistance.' 'By what time?' 'From today, on the seventh day.' 'Very well, let it be so. When your assembly convenes, you must inform me.' The <s>Tīrthyas</s>, their minds anxious and troubled, searched for allies day after day, and counted the days.

Then, when the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> began building a monastery for the Blessed One, the <s>Tīrthyas</s>, their minds agitated with fierce hatred, assembled and approached the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Having approached, they said: 'Do not, householder, build a monastery here for the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>! For what reason? We have divided the cities among us: <s>Rājagṛha</s> belongs to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>; <s>Śrāvastī</s> belongs to us.' He said: 'You may have divided the cities among yourselves, but not my personal property; I shall have a <s>dharma</s>-hall built for whomever I please.' They went to the king. There too they were defeated by <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. The wretched <s>Tīrthyas</s>, with unchanged [defiant] faces, said: 'Householder, we do not freely grant you [permission]. Let the chief disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come; if he defeats us in debate, then build the monastery.' He said: 'Very well; let me first consult the noble <s>Śāriputra</s>.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> approached the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. Having approached, having bowed his head to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>'s feet, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tīrthyas</s> say thus: "Householder, we do not freely grant you [permission]. Let the chief disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come; if he defeats us in debate, then build the monastery." How should we proceed in this matter?' The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'Do these [Tīrthyas] have any roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) or not?' He saw that they did. 'With whom are [those roots] connected?' 'With me.' He reflected further: 'Are only these connected with me as those to be converted, or are there others too who are to be converted through debate?' He saw that there were. 'How long before they will assemble?'

'Just as, householder, a <s>Cakravartin</s> king [travels].' 'With how many [stages] does a <s>Cakravartin</s> king [travel]?' 'A <s>Cakravartin</s> king, householder, travels a road with stages of ten <s>krośas</s>.' There the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> took up a discourse (<s>sūtra</s>) in a secluded place; the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> also took it up in a secluded place. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> began to display a smile. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said: 'Not without cause and condition, noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s> or disciples of the <s>Tathāgata</s> display a smile. What, noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the cause? What is the condition for displaying a smile?' 'Just so, householder, just so. Not without cause and condition do <s>Tathāgatas</s> or disciples of the <s>Tathāgata</s> display a smile. You have taken up a discourse here, and in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven a golden mansion has been produced.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, with eyes wide open in wonder, said: 'Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, if that is so, then please extend the discourse further to an even greater degree; I shall generate even greater faith.' The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> took up that discourse, and the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, to an even greater degree, with an intense surge of faith, generated faith in his mind. By the faith thus generated, immediately that golden mansion was transformed into one made of four kinds of gems. And the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> informed him of this. Thus indeed, <s>bhikṣus</s>, for exclusively black <s>karmas</s>, the result is exclusively black; for exclusively white ones, exclusively white; for mixed ones, mixed. In the past, <s>bhikṣus</s>, a householder lived in a certain market-town — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with extensive and spacious estates, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>'s wealth. When the spring season had arrived, in a grove resounding with the calls of geese, herons, peacocks, parrots, <s>sārikā</s> birds, cuckoos, and <s>jīvajīvaka</s> birds, with its trees in full bloom, he went out to the park grounds with his household. In the absence of the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arise in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, devoted to secluded sleeping-quarters, individually worthy of offerings, [a blessing] to the world. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at that market-town. He stood at a certain spot in that park. The park-keeper informed the householder: 'Sir, at such-and-such a spot, a serene-souled renunciant stands.' Upon hearing this, joy arose in him: 'I am fortunate that such a renunciant is present in my park!' Filled with faith, he set out to see him. That great soul, having entered the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder of clinging (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>), passed into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. had entered the rains retreat. During the rains, a danger arose in that market-town. The <s>bhikṣus</s> dwelling there, frightened and without having completed the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony), came to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. They were given rest by the <s>bhikṣus</s>. When the fatigue of the journey had been relieved, they said: 'Venerable ones, assign us sleeping-quarters.' [The resident monks], thinking 'It is the middle of the rains,' did not assign them. The visiting <s>bhikṣus</s> complained, reproached, and criticized: 'How is it, venerable ones, that you let the Teacher's teaching disappear while the Teacher is still present? If you have any qualms, give sleeping-quarters in order of seniority.' Even so, they did not assign them. The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the Blessed One. On this occasion, the Blessed One said: 'Therefore I prescribe: for <s>bhikṣus</s> whose [retreat] has been broken and disrupted, a second rains-residence entry (<s>varṣopanāyikā</s>) is to be performed.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> did not know how it should be performed. The Blessed One said: 'A three-month <s>pravāraṇā</s> is to be performed; in the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, a second rains-residence entry is to be performed.' The Blessed One had said: 'For <s>bhikṣus</s> whose [retreat] has been broken and disrupted, a second rains-residence entry is to be performed.'
Then other <s>bhikṣus</s> whose [retreat had been] broken and disrupted also came to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'On account of <s>bhikṣus</s> whose [retreat has been] broken and disrupted, I have prescribed a second rains-residence entry, but not a third. <s>Bhikṣus</s> whose [retreat has been] broken and disrupted should be given rest according to their acquaintance.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> made them do work-assignments (<s>karmādāna</s>). The Blessed One said: 'They should not be made to do work-assignments.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> gave them a share of the gains. The Blessed One said: 'A share of the gains should not be given to them.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> did not give them even a share of material goods. The Blessed One said: 'Material goods [may be given] to them, but not a share of cloth [gains].'

) is pleased; the deities become delighted; one accumulates wholesome roots conducive to producing faith; and at the breaking up of the body, one is reborn in a good destiny, in the heavenly world among the gods.' Those who saw that monastery plastered and swept went and informed the householder. He, upon hearing, generated delight. Then on another occasion, he himself came and saw that monastery plastered and swept just the same. He was greatly pleased and covered the alms-begging <s>bhikṣu</s> with a cloth. <s>Upananda</s> heard about this and hastily went and said: 'Alms-beggar, this monastery was assigned to me. Give me the cloth.' The alms-beggar reflected: 'This one is greedy by nature. If I do not give it, he will take it by force anyway and will also expel me from the monastery.' So he handed it over to him. The <s>bhikṣu</s>s reported this matter to the Blessed One. On this occasion the Blessed One said: 'When someone, being pleased, makes an offering out of faith, it belongs to that very [person toward whom the faith was directed]. But <s>Upananda</s>'s is only the rains-retreat share.'
People are fond of virtuous qualities, and even at the cost of great personal hardship to themselves, their sons, and their wives, faithful <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and householders give gifts to those endowed with virtue. They invite forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s>s and feed them. When the forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s>s go to eat in the houses, thieves rob the monasteries. The Blessed One said: 'One should lock the door and take the key before departing.' Thieves used duplicate keys to rob them. The Blessed One said: 'A guard-<s>bhikṣu</s> should be stationed before going. His alms-food should be provided without interruption.' Thieves seized another <s>bhikṣu</s> and brought him [to the door]. He said: 'Open the door.' The Blessed One said: 'A code should be established — "fever" and "no fever." If he says "fever," the door should not be opened. If he says "no fever," it should be opened. Moreover, a forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s> should keep a watchdog (<s>ardhaśākhā</s>).' It was said by the Blessed One: 'A forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s> should keep a watchdog.' The <s>bhikṣu</s>s did not know what kind of watchdog was meant. The Blessed One said: '<s>Bhikṣu</s>s, a watchdog is a dog. The leftover food from the bowl should be given to it.' Forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s>s kept dogs. The dogs scratched the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard and the monastery with their claws and defiled them with excrement and urine. The Blessed One said: 'I shall prescribe, O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, behavioral rules for the dog-keeping

) kukkurapoṣakena bhikṣuṇā kālyam evotthāya stūpāṅgaṇaṃ vihāraś ca pratyavekṣitavyaḥ yan nakharikābhir upalikhitaṃ tat samaṃ kartavyam; uccāraprasrāvaś chorayitavyaḥ, kukkurapoṣako bhikṣur yathāprajñaptān āsamudācārikān dharmān asamādāya vartate, sātisāro vartate
children.translated_text: ) The dog-keeping <s>bhikṣu</s> should rise early in the morning and inspect the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard and the monastery. What has been scratched by claws should be made smooth. Excrement and urine should be cleaned up. If the dog-keeping <s>bhikṣu</s> lives without undertaking the prescribed behavioral rules, he commits a transgression.

When the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having spread coverings worth a <s>koṭi</s>, purchased [the grove] from Prince <s>Jeta</s> and offered it to the <s>Saṅgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, then faithful devotees residing in various regions who worshipped <s>caityas</s> (shrines) came to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Some of them, filled with faith, said: 'Noble ones, we too would like to build something for the noble <s>Saṅgha</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: 'Purchase land with money and build.' 'Noble ones, for how much is it sold?' 'For such-and-such an amount of gold.' 'Noble ones, where would we get so much? But if we could obtain [a place] in this area, we would build.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'The householder should be consulted. If he consents, let it be built.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> consulted the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. He said: 'If faithful <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, on my account, perform meritorious acts for the sake of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, I consent. If they do so for an individual, I do not consent.'
The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'Therefore I prescribe: building may be done for the sake of the <s>Saṅgha</s>. For the sake of an individual, the donor must be consulted. If he consents, it may be built. If he does not consent, it should not be built.'
Visiting <s>bhikṣus</s> who worshipped <s>caityas</s> came to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. They were lodged with <s>bhikṣus</s> according to their acquaintance. Those who had no

) and asked <s>Nanda</s>: 'Noble one, was my cloth taken?' He told him what had happened. The householder, meanwhile, had gone by another path to the forest monastery, distributed the cloths, and departed. <s>Upananda</s> ran back to the forest monastery — but the cloths had already been distributed. Thus, out of excessive greed at both monasteries, he was deprived of his share. He grieved, lamented, and wailed.
The <s>bhikṣu</s>s, seized by doubt, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable One, <s>Upananda</s>, out of excessive greed, has been deprived of a cloth!' The Blessed One said: 'Not only now, O <s>bhikṣu</s>s; in a past life too, out of excessive greed, he lost his food. Listen to this.'

The venerable <s>Upananda</s> was the <s>Saṃgha</s>-elder at a certain monastery. Then another <s>Saṃgha</s>-elder arrived there. <s>Upananda</s> reflected: 'Having been the <s>Saṃgha</s>-elder here, I shall now have to be the second elder. I shall go to another monastery.' He went to another monastery. Then the other elder left that monastery. The second elder's share [now reverted to] the <s>Saṃgha</s>-elder's share. He reflected: 'Here too I would have received the same share; there too I would have received the same share. Why should I give up the <s>Saṃgha</s>-eldership for no reason?' He then hastily set out back to the monastery. He entered the monastery while the lodging-assignments were only half-completed, and said: 'Assign the monastery according to seniority.' The <s>bhikṣu</s>s, considering the time had passed, did not assign. <s>Upananda</s> said: 'Venerable ones, why do you just stand there causing the Teacher's dispensation to vanish? Assign the monastery according to seniority!' The <s>bhikṣu</s>s reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'One who has gone on <s>Saṃgha</s> business, <s>stūpa</s> business, or communal business should have his lodging assigned according to seniority; otherwise, according to order of arrival.'

In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, on both banks of a river there were two monasteries — one for those who ate communal meals (<s>saṃghalābhikas</s>), and a second for those who went for alms (<s>piṇḍapātikas</s>). Now, a certain dog could recognize the sound of the [meal] gong. Hearing the gong, he would go to the communal-meal monastery; those <s>bhikṣus</s> gave him the leftovers from their bowls. Having eaten that, he would go to the alms-goers' monastery, eat the bowl-leftovers there too, and go wherever he pleased. In due course, the alms-goers received an unexpected windfall of food. They sounded the gong at the same time [as the other monastery]. That gong-dog, hearing the gong, began to cross the river. When he had reached midstream, the gong sounded at the communal-meal monastery. His resolve broken, he began to turn back. Carried far by the current, he lost both [meals].
  What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? That gong-dog at that time and occasion was none other than this very <s>Upananda</s>. Then too, through excessive greed, he lost both; now too, through excessive greed, he has lost both. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> should not be excessively greedy. If he does so, it is an offense requiring repentance (<s>sātisāra</s>).

Having approached, he bowed his head to the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable One, visiting <s>bhikṣu</s>s who are unfamiliar with the locality, while going for alms, miss the proper time and end up taking their meal at the base of a wall. Faithless people will use this to disparage the noble ones. If, then, the Blessed One would permit, I would have rest-pavilions built between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and the <s>Jetavana</s>. Wherever it is mealtime for a <s>bhikṣu</s>, he can take his meal there.' The Blessed One said: 'Therefore, householder, I permit it; have them built.' He had rest-pavilions built between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and the <s>Jetavana</s>. Whichever <s>bhikṣu</s> found it to be mealtime wherever, he took his meal there.
Other <s>bhikṣu</s>s lacked drinking water. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> had a well dug there and deposited a cartload of the three pungent substances and the three fruits. That water became delicious and excellent, renowned throughout the land. People heard and came. The <s>bhikṣu</s>s tried to prohibit them. The people of <s>Śrāvastī</s> [said]: 'Noble ones, we attend upon you with all requisites, yet you are withholding water that is common to everyone!' It was a time of scarcity. <s>Bhikṣu</s>s had gone to another monastery. Having seen <s>bhikṣu</s>s eating there, they too desired to eat. Out of scruple, they did not eat. The <s>bhikṣu</s>s reported this matter to the Blessed One. A <s>bhikṣu</s> from the countryside, a <s>caitya</s>-worshipper, came to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, who are knowing and inquiring — they ask knowing, not unknowing; they ask at the right time, not when the time has passed; they ask what is connected with purpose, not what is purposeless; for the <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, the bridge is destroyed regarding purposeless questioning. There, the <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, knowing the right time, ask questions connected with purpose. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, asked the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "What is this, <s>Ānanda</s>, this great uproar at the edge of the park and the noise of a great crowd of people?" He said: "On account of the <s>bhikṣu</s>s <s>Aśvaka</s> and <s>Punarvasuka</s>, three lodging-assigners and six lodging-receivers have been appointed for the <s>bhikṣu</s>s. The <s>bhikṣu</s>s cannot obtain lodging. Therefore this great uproar has arisen at the edge of the park, and the noise of a great crowd of people." The Blessed One said: "<s>Ānanda</s>, the three lodging-assigners and six lodging-receivers were appointed by me with quarrelsome <s>bhikṣu</s>s in mind, not for those who are well-behaved. Therefore, <s>bhikṣu</s>s should not appoint three lodging-assigners and six lodging-receivers for well-behaved <s>bhikṣu</s>s. If they do, they commit a transgression."
